title: Make the reasoning explicit.
prompt: Arrange this complete elementary argument for all fixed points of F(x) = x² on ℝ.
hint: Start from the definition; finish by checking both candidates.

steps.text: Over the real numbers, a product is zero only if at least one factor is zero, so x = 0 or x = 1.
Substitution confirms F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1, so both candidates work and there are no others.
A fixed point x must satisfy x² = x.

feedback.pass: The argument finds every candidate and checks it. This is a worked algebraic proof, not a claim of machine-checked verification.
feedback.fail: Definition → algebra → zero-product reasoning → substitution. A few plotted points would not establish exhaustiveness.
